model: The green space I'd like to describe is Thong Nhat Park, which is a big park in the south of Hanoi, not far from my office. I started going there about two years ago, when a colleague invited me to go for a jog with her after work, and now I go at least three times a week. The park has a large lake in the middle and lots of tree-lined paths, so even in summer it's much cooler than the streets around it. It's also really well looked after. There are gardeners working there every morning, and it's surprisingly clean for such a busy place. What I love most is that it's a chance to get away from the noise. You can hear motorbikes in the distance, but inside it's mostly birds and people chatting. In the early morning you see older people doing tai chi, and in the evening there are kids playing badminton. It's honestly a breath of fresh air after eight hours in front of a screen. When I've had a stressful day, a walk around the lake really helps me clear my head and recharge my batteries. I sometimes think about what would happen if the city sold the land to developers. If they built apartments there, the area would become another concrete jungle, and thousands of people would lose their only green space. So if the city keeps protecting it, I'll keep going there for years.
